cards.subject: Three technologies reach half of American homes
cards.fact: Electric power reached half of American homes in **1925**, 43 years after Pearl Street; the car in **1926**, 40 years after Benz; radio in **1931**, eleven years after KDKA read the Harding election returns.
cards.source: Our World in Data, Comin and Hobijn and others; HUD; FCC
cards.source_short: Our World in Data; HUD; FCC

cards.subject: Television enters the home
cards.fact: **9 percent** of American households had a set in 1950, **65 percent** by 1955 and **87 percent** by 1960, 46 of 53 million homes. Farnsworth had shown electronic television in 1928.
cards.source: US Census Bureau, Census of Housing

cards.subject: Colour, then cable
cards.fact: Colour sets stood in **10 percent** of American homes in 1966 and **57 percent** by 1974. Cable, in a tenth of homes in 1970, reached half by 1985; CNN (1980) and MTV (1981) were cable channels, reachable only through that wire.
cards.source: Our World in Data, Comin and Hobijn and others

cards.subject: The web comes home
cards.fact: A computer stood in **17 percent** of American homes in 1990 and half by 2000. The internet reached a tenth of homes in 1993, two years after Berners-Lee announced the web, and **42 percent** by 2000, the same share that had a mobile phone, up from a tenth in 1994.
cards.source: Our World in Data, Comin and Hobijn and others

cards.subject: Everyone gets online, and the phone comes along
cards.fact: The internet reached half of American homes in 2002 and **74 percent** by 2010. Mobile phones went from **42 to 87 percent** of households, and the landline began its fall, 94 to 75 percent. Social media went from **5 percent** of adults in 2005 to **48 percent** in 2010.
cards.source: Our World in Data, Comin and Hobijn and others

cards.subject: The phone becomes the screen
cards.fact: Smartphones went from **35 percent** of American adults in 2011 to **81 percent** in 2019; social media from **5 percent** in 2005 to half in 2011 and **79 percent** in 2019. Instagram arrived in 2010, Vine lived from 2013 to 2017, TikTok reached a billion users in 2021.
cards.source: Our World in Data, Comin and Hobijn and others; Pew Research Center
cards.source_short: Our World in Data; Pew Research Center

cards.subject: The feed takes the living room
cards.fact: In May 2025 streaming took **44.8 percent** of American television time, more than broadcast and cable together at 44.2, and YouTube alone drew 12.5. That year 54 percent of Americans got news from social media and video networks and 50 percent from television, the first year the order ran that way.

bars.name: Streaming, share of TV time, May 2025

cards.source: Nielsen, The Gauge; Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2025
